name: Beta 0.40.5.187
notes: Ocean worlds: the three openings in the breakwater are the same width, each centred on what passes through it, and the lighthouse now stands a little bigger on its own rocky islet north-east of the refinery.

log.t: Ocean worlds: the three openings in the breakwater are the same width, each centred on what passes through it, and the lighthouse now stands a little bigger on its own rocky islet north-east of the refinery.
Lava is now drawn sharp at any zoom, with a rich glowing crust and molten seams that shift and pulse, and every lava pool, lake and crater throws fountains of molten droplets.
Molten worlds: the plateaus are gone and the small lava pools are now broad lava lakes with crusted, scorched shores, bubbling and spurting all across their surface.

Solar arrays on every world are now detailed sun-tracking panels on metal poles (replacing the terrestrial leaf panels and the ocean buoys): each turns and tilts to follow the sun and lies flat at night.
Terrestrial worlds: desert dunes are painted into the sand instead of standing as 3D shapes, polar snow on the sea no longer ripples, and small stands of trees grow around the base.

Terrestrial worlds: their seas and lakes now use the ocean worlds' water exactly (colours, gloss, swell, crests and glow), the brown uplands are sandy desert with crescent dunes and rippled sand, and no trees grow on the sand.

Sideways lists (tabs, planets, furnace ores) all work the same way: the selected item is centred when you pick it, and once you scroll a list yourself it stays where you left it instead of snapping back.
The icy world hauler no longer has the block-shaped wedge on its nose: its hull now ends in a framed bow plate with two lamps.

Molten worlds: their mountain ranges now use the icy worlds' alpine shapes in basalt and ash, with one peak of each range a volcano holding a lava pool. New molten plateaus carry lava lakes, and all lava (plains, craters, plateaus) drifts, bubbles and spurts like the lava pools. Eruptions work as before.

Derelict freighters reworked: each wreck is a named ship with a story and a last log entry, modelled as a broken freighter with flickering lights, venting gas, sparks, drifting cargo and debris. Tapping it sends a salvage tug from the station to reel in the cargo, and some wrecks hold an ore crate or a navigation core worth star dust.

Events: countdowns sit on the right of the Daily and Weekly events labels, a little more space before an Elite multiplier, and the (i) by a permanent boost scrolls its record into view and turns grey again when closed.

Events: the third mission of the week turns Elite once you've accepted two (no need to complete them first). Elite rewards end with their multiplier in orange, and completed or failed missions keep their objective.
Terrestrial worlds have smaller polar caps, with a narrower band of tundra and patchy snow around them.

Events tab: Daily events and Weekly events labels, each with its countdown in orange. Daily events now show Completed or Failed when over, and every event keeps its reward line: teal when completed, red when failed.

Haulers in finer detail: smoother round parts, panelled hulls, engine bells, vents, antennas, dishes, thrusters and lights. Their glow now fades out as they come in to land or dock, so the detail shows up close.

New haulers: each kind of world now has its own hauler design (an ore hauler, a heat barge, an ice cutter, a scoop tanker, a sea skimmer and an ag freighter), with nav lights and a flame for every engine.
New About page: the Warp tab has an About card next to the user guide, opening the Fair Tap Studios logo, version and the game's fair-play promise.
The flat tops of mesas and buttes on rocky worlds now wear the planet's own skin (its map, cracks and close-up detail), so they match the land around them.
Fix: a mission whose reward you've just claimed now shows the Completed stamp and drops its progress bar, like other completed missions.

Volcanoes: only one erupts at a time on each world, each eruption lasts 10 to 15 seconds, the ash cloud stays lower and drifts off downwind instead of rising straight up, and the tallest volcanoes are shorter.
The haulers are back to their original look: no planet-colour stripe, tinted glow or tail emblem.

World-kit support buildings and finishing touches. The habitat, solar panels, radar and comms spire are built in each world's style: bio-domes, leaf-shaped solar panels and a tree-house radar on terrestrial worlds; panels on buoys, a lattice radar and a striped mast on ocean worlds; hover pods, a floating sensor balloon and a mast of glowing rings on gas giants; frosted domes and radomes and a crystal spire on icy worlds; and heat-shielded buildings with an obsidian spire on molten worlds. Each hauler now wears its planet's colour as a hull stripe and glow, with the Crew Chief's emblem on its tail fin. Glowing ore pulses run down the refinery's pipe to the pad. The rocky control tower has a turning radar, and the rocky refinery's tall stack blows off bursts of exhaust. When a base is on its planet's night side, its windows, trim and pad lights brighten.

Terrestrial worlds: seas and lakes have livelier water (a gentle swell, sun-glints on the crests and foam along the shore), and only real water ripples now, so the polar snow stays still. The poles grade naturally from tundra into a patchy snow fringe and then the snow cap, with a ragged edge and a drifted snow texture.

The cleared ground round the base now blends into the land on rocky, molten, icy and terrestrial worlds: it keeps the surface's own colour, brightness and most of its detail, with a light ground tint and a fine gravel grain, instead of a dull, washed-out patch. Terrestrial bases also stand on rolling meadow, with no snowy peaks under them.
Claiming a planet keeps the view where it is: the zoom level and distance stay the same, so the planet no longer jumps away.

Icy worlds' mountains are rebuilt as crisp alpine ranges: sharp faceted peaks joined by saddle ridges, cut by aretes and gullies, with deep snow on the gentle and high ground, dark rock on steep faces streaked with snow, and blue glacier ice in the valleys.

Ocean worlds' launch pad: the scattered breakwater rocks and loose harbour wall blocks are replaced by a continuous rubble breakwater round the pad, with openings where the conveyor, the refinery pipe and the transit line cross it, and the lighthouse stands on its end.
Ocean worlds no longer have a calmer patch under the base: the full swell runs right under the floating structures.
Gas giants no longer have a cleared patch under the base: the cloud bands and storms run right under the floating structures.
Gas giants' bands are smooth again: the jet streams drift past each other more gently, band edges wave softly instead of zigzagging, and the fine cloud detail is long, even streaks.
A few stars now slowly swell and shrink over a 10 second cycle, each at its own pace.
The Planet tab no longer has a Station orbit card with a Park station here button; park the station from the Station tab.

Terrestrial worlds: the whole base now stands on dry land. The site is scored against every building's footprint, and the low ground round the base is lifted just clear of the sea, so it sits on one continent. Seas and lakes on terrestrial worlds now ripple like an ocean world's water, only calmer.

Floating haulers on ocean worlds and gas giants start their climb well before the works pad, so they no longer clip its edge. On solid worlds the haulers drive up a ramp onto the works pad's deck, and their road is laid out in true distance so they leave the pad by the ramp. The molten launch pad's three blast walls now stand in an arc round its west side. Floating solar panels are back on round decks, sized so they never touch.

Structure fixes: floating haulers on ocean worlds and gas giants rise to the works pad's deck before they cross onto it; the docking-cradle struts over the gas giants' launch pad are gone; every floating structure on gas giants has lift thrusters under its deck, like the launch pad's; the habitat sits a little further north and its walkway passes between the silos; the solar blocks are spaced so they no longer overlap (and float on their own rectangular decks); and the refinery's pipes end in a pump house by the pad and valve boxes at the refinery, so they always connect.

Every structure now meets the ground properly. Flat footings, pads and dome bases are deepened so their edges no longer float above the curve of the planet. The landing pad's hangars, towers, tanks, lights and breakwaters sit down on the ground. Every raised pipe, walkway and conveyor has supports in its world's style: steel, heat-shielded, insulated or timber trestles, floats on ocean worlds, and glowing hover nodes on gas giants.

The mine is simplified. Haulers tip their ore at a detailed unloading station in the centre of a new mine works pad, built in each world's own materials. A single covered conveyor runs from it to the garage, which is back on the mine head, and the garage's conveyor to the landing pad is restored. The ore yard, the long pipes and the bunker are gone, and the refinery is back in its old place, piped to the pad. Each world's own works (pit, derrick, rig, harvester ring or pond) stand beside the pad. On terrestrial and ocean worlds every hauler's route is planned over the real terrain: walkers keep to land and skimmers keep to water.

The mine is rebuilt around the mine works. The ore deposits are now far out across the planet and spread wide, so miners make long drives on their own track roads. They tip their loads into a hopper in a new ore yard at the works, and the trip times follow the drive. A conveyor on trestles carries the ore to the refinery, which now stands beside the works (an ore bunker holds its place until the Shift Crew arrives), and a pipe takes it on to the pad. The yard adds a stockpile with the second crew, and a crusher house and control tower with the third. The garage is gone: the mine head is now the operations centre. The close-up frames the colony toward the works.

Molten worlds: lava pools have irregular, lumpy outlines; the ore deposits, the magma channel and the taps at the mine now hold the same dark-crusted molten lava as the pools on the plains; and the deposits are spread further apart.
Vegetation worlds are now called Terrestrial worlds everywhere in the game.
